item.title: USDA Staffing Crisis: A Year of Losses and the Road Ahead
item.description: The post wraps up NSAC's multi-part series documenting unprecedented staffing losses at USDA in 2025. Nearly 18,000 employees departed amid buyouts and separations, severely weakening the department’s ability to deliver conservation, farm loan, food safety, research, and rural development services just as farmers face mounting economic and climate pressures. item.title: Guest Post: Thinking like a prairie - strategies for perennial conservation
item.description: The guest blog post explores how mimicking prairie ecosystems through perennial agricultural practices can restore soil health, protect water, support biodiversity, and build climate resilience. Using Wisconsin as a case study, it highlights that although these practices receive a limited share of conservation funding, skilled and passionate conservation staff play a crucial role in directing resources and helping farmers adopt prairie-like systems.

item.title: Comment: Farm Assistance Framework Signals Need and Opportunity to Build More Robust Support
item.description: NSAC welcomed the House Agriculture Committee Minority’s farm assistance framework as a timely response to mounting financial pressures on farmers, while emphasizing that robust relief is long overdue. NSAC called on Congress to build on the framework with inclusive, comprehensive support that keeps farmers on the land and addresses both immediate financial needs and long-term market and cost challenges.

item.title: Release: 500 Farmers Urge Congress to Act Amid Growing Farm Crisis
item.description: A coalition of 500 farmers and ranchers delivered a letter to Congress urging immediate action to address the worsening farm crisis marked by high production costs, volatile markets, low prices, and overproduction. The letter calls for comprehensive, long-term investments in domestic markets, local supply chains, conservation practices, and financial assistance to prevent foreclosures and ensure the long-term viability of farms and rural communities.

item.title: Release: Farmers and Advocates Converge in DC for NSAC Lobby Day
item.description: Nearly 150 farmers, ranchers, and food system advocates from Alaska to Florida, joined NSAC in Washington, DC to press for action on federal agriculture and food policy. Participants held more than 150 meetings with members of Congress, congressional staff, and USDA, nearly doubling farmer participation from recent years and underscoring mounting frustration across farm country.

item.title: Comment: In Moment of Need, House Farm Bill Underdelivers with Empty Promises
item.description: The House draft of the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 fails to provide meaningful investments or reforms, weakens conservation funding, and leaves key programs effectively cut due to inflation. While the bill includes potential improvements for local and regional food systems, the lack of mandatory funding and broader support falls short of what farmers and communities actually need.

item.title: At a Crossroads, House Farm Bill Falls Unmistakably Short
item.description: The Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, introduced by the House Agriculture Committee, fails to meet the urgent needs of farmers amid widespread financial instability, USDA contract freezes, and deep cuts to nutrition programs, offering mostly flat funding that effectively amounts to cuts after inflation. item.description: NSAC convened over 150 farmers and advocates in Washington, DC for its 2026 Winter Meeting, where participants strategized around shared policy priorities and met with members of Congress and USDA officials during our Hill Day, elevating farmer-led solutions during a challenging moment for sustainable agriculture. item.title: Comment: Without Investments and Reforms, House Bill Rings Hollow
item.description: The House Agriculture Committee’s passage of the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 maintains the status quo and relies on largely unfunded authorizations rather than making meaningful reforms or investments to better support farmers. NSAC urges Congress to pursue a bipartisan farm bill that provides real funding, strengthens opportunities for small and mid-sized farmers, and supports resilient farming communities.

item.title: Unpacking the House Farm Bill: Part 1
item.description: The House Agriculture Committee passed the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 after a lengthy, amendment-heavy markup, but budget constraints and partisan divides led to many proposed improvements being rejected. While the bill includes some positive elements, it largely fails to address major agricultural challenges and faces an uncertain path forward without bipartisan support and new funding.
